carousels.title: Custom, or template?

slides.sub: We pick per project. And the answer is 'template' more often than any agency will tell you.

slides.body: Marketing sites. Brochures. Small commerce with a clean flow. If the design isn't the value driver, template is the honest quote.

slides.body: The homepage IS the pitch. The product page is where the deal is won. Performance is load-bearing. The integration surface is non-trivial. Then custom earns its price.

Whether the client is 'important enough' for custom
The agency's default preference
'Everyone else is on custom'

carousels.title: Four caches. Most sites configure one.

slides.headline:
Caches. Most sites
configure one.
slides.sub: Which is why installing WP Rocket alone doesn't fix a slow site.

slides.title: The one you probably have
slides.body: Page cache. The whole rendered HTML for a URL, saved and served without touching PHP or the database. WP Rocket handles this by default. It's the first layer, not the last.

slides.title: Browser cache
slides.body: Headers that tell the visitor's browser 'keep this image, this CSS, this font for a week.' Costs nothing to configure. Most sites leave it at default and pay for it on every return visit.

slides.title: Object cache
slides.body: Database query results held in memory (Redis or Memcached). This is the one that separates a fast dashboard from a slow one. The one most WordPress sites completely skip.

slides.title: CDN cache
slides.body: Static assets served from a server near your visitor instead of near your host. Turns a Vancouver site into an instant site in Vancouver, London and Sydney.

slides.headline: How many of the four does your site have?
slides.sub: Comment the count. Under three, we tell you which layer is the fastest win from where you are now.
